solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pound is given to me in immediate part-payment

indicators.note: in tells us the pound sign and me go inside the word for immediate

parts.note: immediate means instant
L is the abbreviation for pound (libra)
taken as written

explanation.surface: A creditor demands money be handed over at once as a first portion of a debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like a verb, as in hammering, but it is the abbreviation L for the pound sterling; 'is given to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An instalment is one of several portions in which a sum is paid off.

clue.text: Ones for reform — yet they vote against

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so the letters of Ones are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some people want change, yet still oppose it in a ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for reform' shuffles ONES; 'yet' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In a division of Parliament the votes against are counted as the opposing side.

clue.text: Part of a head place of worship

explanation.surface: A part of the skull doubles as a sacred building.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat side of the skull beside the eye shares its name with a building for worship.

clue.text: Give generously when there's a whip-round?

explanation.surface: Being generous when colleagues pass the hat round for a collection.
explanation.walkthrough: A whip-round is a collection among friends, but read literally a whip is lashed out.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend lavishly is a common informal phrase, and literally describes swinging a whip.

clue.text: Live wildly in sin

indicators.note: living wildly suggests disorder, so the letters of Live are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone leads a dissolute life of sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Wickedness or sin is a noun synonym of wrongdoing.

clue.text: One's cut out for the religious life

definitions.text: One's cut out for the religious life

parts.words: One's cut out for the religious life
parts.note: read as hair shaved from a monk's crown on entering holy orders, not a person suited to the cloister

explanation.definitionFit: A monk's shaven patch on the crown is literally cut when entering religious life.

clue.text: Too tough for soldiers to break through

definitions.text: Too tough for soldiers to break through

parts.words: Too tough for soldiers to break through
parts.note: soldiers here are strips of toast dipped into a soft egg, which cannot pierce a firmly cooked one

explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers are, in Britain, fingers of toast dunked into a soft-boiled egg.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg cooked solid cannot be dipped; the term also means tough and unsentimental.

clue.text: Studies hijacking plot

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or peruse
piracy covers the hijacking of ships or aircraft

explanation.surface: A secret study of how to seize an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a secret plan by a group to do something unlawful.

clue.text: The prosecutor has to act — see foot of column

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor
to do means to act

explanation.surface: A lawyer acts, and the reader is directed to the bottom of a newspaper column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see foot of column' looks like a newspaper cross-reference but is an architectural definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Architecturally, the plinth or lower part of a pedestal under a column bears this name.

clue.text: Leave the wrong impression

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters of impression are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Departing gives people a mistaken idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave in the sense of authorisation, as in asking leave to speak.

clue.text: Various colours for sunglasses

explanation.surface: A range of tints offered for dark glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Variations of a hue are its tones; informally, dark spectacles are known by the same word.

clue.text: Motor takes on fresh fuel, being cautious

parts.note: a motor is a car

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters of fuel are made into a new order

explanation.surface: A vehicle fills up with new petrol, carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes on' simply joins the pieces; 'fresh' rearranges FUEL as EFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wary and avoiding risk is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Brown's competence in the garden

parts.note: refers to the nickname of Lancelot Brown, the 18th-century English landscape gardener, which is also a word for ability

explanation.walkthrough: Lancelot Brown was a famous English landscape gardener known by a nickname meaning ability.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means ability or competence, and was the gardener Brown's famous nickname.

clue.text: Control said to be restored

parts.note: a rein controls a horse, so to rein is to control
stated means said

explanation.surface: Authority is declared to have been brought back.
explanation.definitionFit: Put back into a former position or condition, synonymous with reinstalled.

clue.text: Ease off the downward pressure?

explanation.surface: Relieving the push from above.
explanation.definitionFit: To slacken is a phrasal verb meaning ease; read literally, releasing pressure lifts it upward.

clue.text: Oil change needed after expedition in N Africa

indicators.note: this word only joins the neighbouring pieces: it says which one stands next to which in the answer

parts.note: a trip is a journey or expedition

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of Oil are altered in order

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: After a journey in North Africa you need an oil change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges OIL as OLI. The definition is a place 'in N Africa', the Libyan capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Libya's capital city lies on the North African coast.

clue.text: Persuade an agency girl to start typing

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker supplied by an agency

indicators.note: to start means the opening letter of typing is taken

explanation.surface: Coaxing a temporary secretary into beginning her typing.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice or coax someone into doing something.

clue.text: The inclusion of two similar points produces a titter

indicators.note: inclusion of means one point is placed within the word The

parts.note: taken as written
E is east, a compass point; two such points supply two Es
E is east, a compass point; two such points supply two Es

explanation.surface: Adding a couple of matching marks to a word makes someone giggle.
explanation.walkthrough: One E goes inside THE (giving TEHE) and the other follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nervous suppressed laugh, the sound of a giggle.

clue.text: I knock back about a couple

indicators.note: about means the turned knock surrounds the letter I
back means the word for knock is read the other way

parts.note: a rap is a knock

explanation.surface: I hit back at a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RAP into PAR, which goes 'about' I.
explanation.definitionFit: Two of something make a couple or a duo.

clue.text: Expert returns to place of exile

indicators.note: returns tells us the word for expert is read from right to left

parts.note: an expert is able, skilled

explanation.surface: A skilled person goes back to where they were banished.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was exiled to this Mediterranean island in 1814.

clue.text: Makes a hit in Oxbridge sporting contest

explanation.surface: Someone scores a hit in a university sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge, bumps are rowing races where boats try to touch the boat ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock into is to collide; the college rowing races are named for those collisions.

clue.text: Brace of fresh lobster

indicators.note: fresh suggests a new arrangement of the letters of lobster

explanation.surface: Two of a freshly caught shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brace' tempts as a pair; it is the verb to support. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To support or reinforce something, as a brace does.

clue.text: Give way and die

explanation.surface: Yielding and dying.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield to pressure, and also to die from illness or injury.

clue.text: Stage at which one may get on

definitions.text: Stage at which one may get on

parts.words: Stage at which one may get on
parts.note: suggests a point in a career for advancement, but is a fare stage where passengers board a vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: A roadside halt where passengers board public transport.

clue.text: Time to arrange sea-duty

indicators.note: to arrange means the letters of sea-duty are reordered

explanation.surface: It is time to organise naval service.
explanation.definitionFit: A day of the week is a period of time.

clue.text: Stable form of electricity

explanation.surface: A steady charge of electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: Unchanging or stationary, and the charge that builds on surfaces without flowing.

clue.text: Discovers money makes money

parts.note: L stands for pound, a unit of money
to earn is to make money

explanation.surface: Someone finds out that wealth begets wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: To find out or come to know something is to acquire knowledge.

clue.text: The responsibility we bear?

explanation.surface: A duty that we ourselves must carry.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden or duty; split in two words it says something rests upon ourselves.

clue.text: Player must be included in the top eleven of all time

indicators.note: included in signals that the name sits inside the words top eleven

explanation.surface: A footballer must be picked for the all-time greatest team.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brazilian footballer is in 'toP ELEven'; 'of all time' adds to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brazilian striker is one of football's most famous players.

clue.text: Language bound to make one embarrassed and speechless

parts.note: a tongue is a language
tied means bound

explanation.surface: A language that leaves someone flustered and lost for words.
explanation.definitionFit: Unable to speak through shyness or embarrassment.

clue.text: One who draws level

parts.note: a person who ties the score, and the word is also a row or level itself

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who ties a match, and also a row or layer in a series of levels.

clue.text: Trek bus cut out, dangerous to drive?

indicators.note: out implies the letters of Trek bus cut are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A trekking bus is taken off the road because it is unsafe.
explanation.definitionFit: A decrepit, corroded old car may well be unsafe to drive.
